title: Formal plane-equation calculation of the adjunction lattice
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $S$ be a reduced finite-type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], with $\operatorname{Spec}S$ pure of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension] and a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Let $\mathfrak m$ be a maximal ideal with residue field $k$, put $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and let $K_A$ be the stalk of the adjunction line of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction]. Write $Q(A)$ for $A$ with all non-zero-divisors inverted and $B\subset Q(A)$ for its integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Let $D=B_{\mathfrak n}$ at a maximal ideal over $\mathfrak m$, and assume that $D$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], is essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], has residue field $k$, and is the local ring of a smooth curve [def-sc-curves]. Let $F$ be its fraction field. On the generic point of this branch the smooth-locus identification of the adjunction line defines an isomorphism $K_A\otimes_A F\cong\Omega^1_{F/k}$, where differentials are [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

Suppose an isomorphism of complete local $k$-algebras $\widehat A\cong k[[x,y]]/(f)$ is given, where $f\neq0$ belongs to $(x,y)$ and this quotient is reduced; completion is maximal-ideal-adic [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and formal power series are [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Choose a complete local $k$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat D\cong k[[t]]$; the map $\widehat A\to\widehat D$ gives $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t)$. Assume the images of $f_x=\partial f/\partial x$ and $f_y=\partial f/\partial y$ in $k[[t]]$ are not both zero. Formal differentiation means $\mathrm d(\sum a_nt^n)=\sum n a_nt^{n-1}\mathrm dt$, extended to $k((t))$ by the quotient rule; the partial derivatives are defined coefficientwise in the same way. Under the map of rational differentials $\Omega^1_{F/k}\to k((t))\mathrm dt$ induced by $F\hookrightarrow k((t))$, the image of the completed $D$-span $(K_A\otimes_A D)\otimes_D k[[t]]$ (extension of scalars [def-weil-module-base-change]) is the free rank-one $k[[t]]$-lattice generated by
$$
 r=\frac{x'(t)\,\mathrm dt}{f_y(x(t),y(t))}\quad\text{if }f_y(x(t),y(t))\neq0,
 \qquad
 r=-\frac{y'(t)\,\mathrm dt}{f_x(x(t),y(t))}\quad\text{if }f_x(x(t),y(t))\neq0.
$$
The formulas agree when both denominators are nonzero. In this comparison the completed regular-differential module $\Omega^1_{D/k}\otimes_D k[[t]]$ is $k[[t]]\mathrm dt$. The lattice is compared through the given generic smooth-locus identification; thus it is independent of the chosen algebraic presentation, the formal equation, and the formal parameter.

source.place: Tag 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci), determinant/conormal calculation in its proof; completion-compatible formal plane-equation formulation of that calculation. This formulation is an agent-specified auxiliary statement, not a verbatim assertion of the tag.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-domain], $k[[x,y]]$ is a domain. Thus $f\ne0$ is a nonzerodivisor, and $f\in(x,y)$ makes its quotient nonzero; $f$ is a regular sequence of length one by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Apply [lem-trf-completed-conormal-determinant-comparison] with $d=1,n=2,c=1$: $k$ is perfect, $S$ has the required reduced lci pure-dimensional hypotheses, its maximal residue field is $k$, and $R=\widehat A$ is reduced by the given formal presentation. We obtain the specified isomorphism $K_A\otimes_A R\cong\lambda_f=(R\bar f)^\vee\otimes_R\bigwedge^2(R\,\mathrm dx\oplus R\,\mathrm dy)$. Its normalization square applies to $R\to L=k((t))$: the restriction to $A$ factors through the given smooth generic point of the normalization branch. It identifies the inverse formal determinant map with the given algebraic generic differential map. This is the required completion comparison; base change of $S$ is not being used.

source.place: Auxiliary formal comparison for Tag 0E9Z; no source-completion assertion is taken from Tag 0E2Y.

proof.text: Choose the generator $\varepsilon=-\bar f^\vee\otimes(\mathrm dx\wedge\mathrm dy)$ of $\lambda_f$. In $L$ put $a=f_x(x(t),y(t))$ and $b=f_y(x(t),y(t))$. The formal conormal differential sends $\bar f$ to $a\,\mathrm dx+b\,\mathrm dy$. The normalized determinant map of [lem-trf-completed-conormal-determinant-comparison] sends $\mathrm dx$ to $-b\,\bar f^\vee\otimes(\mathrm dx\wedge\mathrm dy)=b\varepsilon$, and $\mathrm dy$ to $a\,\bar f^\vee\otimes(\mathrm dx\wedge\mathrm dy)=-a\varepsilon$. Consequently its inverse sends $\varepsilon$ to $\mathrm dx/b$ if $b\ne0$, or to $-\mathrm dy/a$ if $a\ne0$. At least one is allowed by hypothesis. These inversions take place in $L$, so no partial derivative is required to be a unit in $k[[t]]$.

source.place: Determinant wedge formula preceding Tag 0E9Z, with the normalization supplied by the separately stated comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-completed-jacobian-differentials] separately to $D$. The assumption that $D$ is the local ring of a smooth curve at a point with residue $k$ supplies a localization of an affine finite-type $k$-algebra at that maximal ideal. The coefficient section is the structural map from $k$, and the chosen presentation is $\widehat D=k[[t]]$, with one variable and no equations. The lemma therefore identifies $\Omega^1_{D/k}\otimes_D k[[t]]$ with $k[[t]]\,\mathrm dt$, with the continuous extension of $d_D$ sending $t$ to $\mathrm dt$. On polynomials it is termwise differentiation by the derivation rule. Continuity and polynomial truncations give $d_D^\wedge(h(t))=h'(t)\,\mathrm dt$ for every power series. The quotient rule $d(a/b)=b^{-1}da-ab^{-2}db$ extends every derivation of $D$ uniquely to $F$ with values in an $F$-module; the universal property therefore gives $\Omega^1_{D/k}\otimes_D F=\Omega^1_{F/k}$. Localizing the completed identification to $L$ now shows that the scalar extension of the rational-differential map $\Omega^1_{F/k}\to L\,\mathrm dt$ is an isomorphism; thus a nonzero rational differential stays nonzero.

source.place: Tag 0C4D, completed-Jacobian comparison applied with one variable and no equations to the smooth branch DVR.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-completed-jacobian-differentials] also to $A$ and its plane presentation. The completed algebraic differential cokernel has coordinate classes $\widehat d_A(x),\widehat d_A(y)$. The algebraic differential map for $A\to D$ commutes with universal derivations by [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. After completing, the induced derivation on $R$ and the composite $R\to\widehat D\xrightarrow{d_D^\wedge}k[[t]]\,\mathrm dt$ agree on the dense subring $A$. Both are continuous into the separated module $k[[t]]\,\mathrm dt$, so they agree on $R$. Hence $\mathrm dx\mapsto x'(t)\,\mathrm dt$ and $\mathrm dy\mapsto y'(t)\,\mathrm dt$. By steps 1--2 the completed adjunction generator maps to $x'(t)\,\mathrm dt/b$, respectively $-y'(t)\,\mathrm dt/a$. Associativity of tensor extension [def-weil-module-base-change] identifies its $k[[t]]$-span with the image of $(K_A\otimes_A D)\otimes_D k[[t]]$. This generator is nonzero by step 3 and the generic isomorphism in step 1, so its span is a free rank-one lattice.

source.place: Tag 0E9Z residue calculation following the formal comparison, with explicit continuous pullback of the differential classes.

proof.text: The relation $f_x\,\mathrm dx+f_y\,\mathrm dy=0$ in the completed differential cokernel of [lem-trf-completed-jacobian-differentials], mapped as in step 4, gives $a x'(t)+b y'(t)=0$. If $a,b$ are both nonzero, division by $ab$ gives $x'(t)/b=-y'(t)/a$. Thus the two displayed fractions agree.

source.place: The conormal relation in the determinant calculation of Tag 0E9Z.

proof.text: For any other algebraic presentation or regular formal presentation of the same $R$, the comparison and generic-normalization identities of [lem-trf-completed-conormal-determinant-comparison] identify the resulting image with the same completed algebraic line inside rational differentials. Thus their lattices agree; we are using formal-presentation compatibility explicitly. For a change $t=t(s)$ of the complete branch parameter, [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-coordinate-chain-rule] in one variable gives the chain rule and the invertibility of $t'(s)$. Substitution sends $\mathrm dt$ to $t'(s)\,\mathrm ds$ and the two residue expressions to the corresponding expressions in $s$. This is an invertible identification of the ambient regular differential modules and of the calculated lattices, proving the stated parameter independence.

source.place: Tag 0C4B coordinate changes, together with the formal determinant comparison and its generic normalization.
